sentences.text: CNN, Politico and MS NOW are back in the White House, hours after a federal judge ruled President Donald Trump's ban on the three news outlets was probably unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored.
sentences.article_title: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order

sentences.text: The outlets sought an emergency court hearing to regain entry accusing the White House in a court filing of having "repeatedly violated" the judge's ruling by turning away their journalists.

sentences.text: The hearing was called off after access was restored.
sentences.article_title: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order

sentences.text: Trump initially said he barred the outlets because of "fake news".
sentences.article_title: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order

sentences.text: The White House later cited national security.
sentences.article_title: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order

sentences.text: But in his overnight ruling, Judge Timothy Kelly cast doubt on the claim about national security concerns.
sentences.article_title: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order

sentences.text: The chaotic standoff limited some TV coverage as Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House ahead of a state dinner later.

sentences.text: Shortly afterwards, all three outlets said they were allowed back in.

sentences.text: This video can not be played A red carpet and military flyover - How Trump welcomed Xi At least so far, Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington has been all pomp and little obvious progress on pressing issues.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: From the ceremonial welcoming at a military air base on Wednesday to the honour-guard arrival at the White House this morning, President Donald Trump rolled out the red carpet – literally and figuratively – for his Chinese counterpart.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: The public remarks from the two leaders have teemed with warm words and diplomatic niceties.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: In a statement before today's formal meetings, Xi announced a gift of Chinese pandas and unveiled a new student exchange programme.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "Let us keep advancing the cause of friendship between our two peoples and work together to build a better world," he said.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: Trump, for his part, outlined some of the topics the leaders planned to discuss in their meetings, including "pressing issues concerning security, technology, and superintelligence" - using his preferred term for artificial intelligence.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: Trump says he and Xi held 'great meeting' as Chinese leader visits White House "The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come," he said.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: The marching bands and military flyovers on Thursday may serve a larger purpose, however – at least for Trump.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "This is a little bit of intentional pageantry to talk up the positive vibes of the summit," Jennifer Welch, chief economic analyst for Bloomberg Economics, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "This is very much how President Trump sees the summit and the role he plays in the US-China relationship, as ballast to provide stability." Even so, there is still an edge to some of Xi's rhetoric, she notes.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: In remarks at the White House, the Chinese leader again mentioned the "Thucydides trap" – a theory that shifts in global power tend to lead to conflict between rising and declining nations.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "China and the United States are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialogue, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust," Xi said.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: The obstacles in the way of reaching any substantive agreement between the two nations are significant, however.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: When Trump and Xi met in Beijing in May, the men agreed to form boards of trade and investment to oversee economic interactions, and little more.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: On Wednesday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a year-long trade "truce" between the two nations that had kept tariffs lower would be extended another two months.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: Financial analysts expect a further extension could come before this week's summit ends, given that neither side wants a renewal of last year's trade war.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: The outlook for progress is much dimmer on other topics, like the US war with Iran, the Ukraine war and regulating AI.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: China's reneging on promises to buy more American agricultural products and to also sell more rare earth minerals to the US is helping cloud the outlook.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: China, meanwhile, is watching to see if Trump follows through on a proposed sale of American weapons to Taiwan, which has been on hold for months.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Here's why Trump's been so keen on Xi's visit When it comes to AI, China and the US have two very different goals for any agreement on the race to develop the technology, Robyn Klingler-Vida, a professor of political economy at Kings College London, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "On the US side, it's about existential risk and slowing down AI potentially," she said.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "Whereas in China, it's about acceleration, maybe winning the AI tech race and the application of AI to the real economy." sentences.text: Muscle-flexing aside, more pageantry – and the promise of stability – may be the end result of Xi's China visit, even with additional face time between the two leaders to come before Xi departs on Friday afternoon.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: "What China talks about is metaphysical and abstract.
sentences.article_title: Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

sentences.text: Complaints about the broadcast of a swear word in connection with Victoria Beckham during an episode of BBC One's Have I Got News For You have been upheld, the corporation's executive complaints unit (ECU) has ruled.
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: The show, from 7 November last year, hosted by comic and presenter Katherine Ryan, featured an email allegedly sent by Sir David Beckham in which the word was used.
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: The ECU finding has been reported to the management of BBC Content.
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: As a result, a version of the programme edited in light of the finding will replace the version currently on iPlayer.
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: The ECU statement in full said: "The relevant BBC Editorial Guidelines do not require programmes to avoid giving offence, but do require that any offence should be editorially justified.
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: It said "the use of the strong language was editorially justified as the panel were discussing a current news story about Sir David Beckham and directly quoting from leaked emails in which he had used the word in question, leading to further discussion".
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: It added that it was "common practice" to carry a clear verbal warning at the start of post-watershed programmes with very strong language, which was what happened for this particular episode of the show.
sentences.article_title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You

sentences.text: "It is never our intention to offend our audience," the statement added.

sentences.text: Ahead of agreeing to expand the review to cases dating back to 2015, members of the trust's board offered "sincere" apologies for the failings and harm caused.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: At an extraordinary meeting of the board held in Durham, board chair Alison Marshall said: "I would like to offer a sincere apology to all the women and their families who have been affected by the failings in our breast services.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: "I can't imagine the impact that has had." She said they could "not turn back the clock" but would be "open, honest and transparent" about the failings.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Chief nurse Gill Hunt told the board concerns were first raised in 2015 after a "service reconfiguration" and loss of breast surgical trainee posts.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Over the following years patients and bodies such as the Northern Cancer Alliance, Care Quality Commission and NHS England raised multiple issues, she said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The key "themes" included treatment "not aligned to best practice", excessive surgery and delayed diagnosis, she said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The trust's breast surgery lookback review began in April 2025 by examining cases between January 2023 and February 2025.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Hunt said 538 cases had been reviewed so far with 321 having experienced some form of harm, including one death.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The trust has been reviewing breast cancer care at its hospitals and services in County Durham and Darlington About 640 patients had also contacted a special helpline asking for their cases to be reviewed, the board heard.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The review cost about £523,000 in its first year and involved nine reviewers looking at about 80 cases a month, the report said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The board agreed to extend the review by one year at a time back to 2015, which would encompass up to 4,500 further cases and take an estimated five years to complete.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Hunt said the expanded review would "provide a proportionate and evidence-led clinical approach" in response to "emerging findings", while decisions would be "supported by clear clinical rationale and formal governance review".
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Other "important learning" to come out of the review so far was about how bosses should respond to concerns raised by patients or other agencies, Hunt said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: "We are committed to doing the right thing," she said.

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: He also said the trust was currently exceeding national standards for breast cancer treatment, including for the number of women having breast conservation surgeries and being offered immediate reconstruction.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: "None of that changes what has happened to women in the past but hopefully gives confidence the changes made in the service have had an impact on the outcomes," Russell said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: He said patients today could be "confident" they would be "treated appropriately" and get "good clinical outcomes".
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The helpline, which is available by phone or email, would remain open with any concerned patients encouraged to contact it "irrespective" of when they were treated, he said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Denise was one of the women who had an unnecessary mastectomy Denise Howarth attended the board meeting along with other patients.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: The 51-year-old from Consett, County Durham, who had an unnecessary mastectomy, said she was "pleased" the review would be extended as there could be many more cases still to be revealed.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: But past patients needed to be contacted with "dignity" and "compassion", she added, to try and reduce the "shock" and "pain" of being told their cases were being reviewed because of possible failings.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: She also said she thought the review would find more women harmed "than what they are predicting".
sentences.article_title: NHS trust to review 4,500 breast cancer cases after unnecessary surgeries found

sentences.text: Waiting for their cases to be reviewed would cause "further anxiety and trauma" for many, she said, adding: "Justice delayed is justice denied." She also said the review should look further back than 2015 while a full public inquiry was the "only way proper scrutiny and full accountability can be achieved".

sentences.text: Maricarmen had to leave the flat she had lived in for 70 years on Wednesday The dramatic eviction of an 87-year-old woman from the home in Madrid where she lived for seven decades has drawn attention to the depth of Spain's housing crisis.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

sentences.article_title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

sentences.text: Maricarmen's father first rented the property in 1956 and she continued as the tenant after her parents died, during which time there was a cap on the rent.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

sentences.text: However, the company that bought the property in 2018, Urbagestión, cited a legal glitch allowing it to raise her rent from €500 (£428; $572) to €2,650.

sentences.text: It subsequently lowered the new rent to €1,650 but Maricarmen was still unable to pay it with her monthly pension of €1,350.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

sentences.text: Three previous attempts to evict her were blocked by the courts and the case has received increasing media attention.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

sentences.article_title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

sentences.text: India's opposition parties have demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign from office India's Election Commission (ECI) is facing yet another crisis of credibility after a series of fresh allegations of irregularities against its chief.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: One of the most trusted public institutions in the world's largest democracy, the three-member commission is headed by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and includes Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as commissioners.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The latest row broke out after a report in the Indian Express newspaper , external said that in the past few months, CEC Kumar had been repeatedly questioned by his two colleagues over the integrity of the voter database, changes to the way new voters are enrolled and the security of the electoral rolls itself.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The report said that Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi objected to several decisions which were taken without their knowledge.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: There were at least 14 times in the past 10 months when Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi were kept in the dark, it added.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: In one instance, the report says, the two commissioners even wrote a letter complaining to the chief secretary, the top bureaucrat in the Indian government.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The revelations have created a furore, with opposition leaders demanding Kumar's resignation.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: Sandhu and Joshi have not publicly commented on the report but the ECI said in a statement that "differing views" were part of the "decision-making process".
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The report comes at a time when the commission is carrying out a controversial country-wide revision of the electoral database.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The Election Commission says the aim of this Special Intensive Revision - better known by its acronym SIR - is to ensure that no ineligible name remains on the rolls.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: It says the last revision was done nearly a quarter of a century ago and the voters' list needs to be updated to account for those who have died, left the country or are registered in more than one place as they've moved to a new address.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: But the exercise has been mired in controversy from the start with the opposition parties accusing CEC Kumar of manipulating voters' list to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during elections.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: But the latest revelations are being seen as much more serious as they are about questions being raised from within the Election Commission about the way its chief is functioning.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The Indian Express report says that CEC Kumar has been repeatedly questioned by his two colleagues over the integrity of the voter database in recent months From the start, questions have lingered over the robustness of the revision, which has seen 130 million names from across India struck off the voters' list.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: Millions of voters have also complained to the authorities that their names are missing, saying the new process set by SIR to register as voters is too cumbersome and involves furnishing documents that many don't have.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: Former CEC SY Quraishi, who says he has "been a critic of the SIR from the beginning", told news agency PTI that he always wondered why Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had been "keeping quiet".
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: "[Now] I realised that very silently and quietly they were protesting, they were writing notes.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: That is a good thing, they have gone up in my esteem," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: On Wednesday, angry opposition politicians once again questioned the sanctity of India's election process and demanded that CEC Kumar resign, saying he had no right to continue in office, with some even calling for his arrest.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The charge was led by MP and senior Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi who has repeatedly accused the Commission of "stealing votes from the opposition".
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: On Wednesday, he also accused the Commission and its officers of "treason".
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: "Vote chori [theft] is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The BJP, RSS [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh] and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: Justice will be served," he posted on X , external .
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: He also shared a 15-second video telling the commission and its officers that "your time will come.
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: At least 2.7million voters were removed in the state during SIR - Banerjee and her supporters say that cost them dozens of seats and the election win.

sentences.text: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has repeatedly accused the commission of "stealing votes from the opposition" Within hours of the Indian Express report and statements from opposition leaders, the Election Commission put out a statement , external defending its way of working.

sentences.text: "Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution.

sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: The note said that highlighting "certain specific internal notes and observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives" give only part of the picture.

sentences.text: And that in recent months, the commission has "introduced around 40 new initiatives and undertaken many electoral reforms including the conduct of electoral roll revision (including SIR) across the country.

sentences.text: Party spokesperson Sambit Patra told a press conference that "ever since the Modi government came to power in 2014, opposition parties have been collapsing one after the other".
sentences.article_title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again

sentences.text: And because they cannot win elections, they are trying to "undermine the institutions of the country", he said.

sentences.text: And India's influential Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which recently forced the education minister to resign, has also said it will protest against the "hijacking of India's democracy".

sentences.text: Analysts say the defence of the Election Commission is unlikely to satisfy many, with some pointing out that its statement doesn't address all the issues raised in the newspaper report and that "CEC Kumar needs to clear the air , external if we are to view the Commission as an impartial body".

sentences.text: (Left to right) Rosa Sharkey, Sarah Foy and Rose Patterson, pictured outside Norwich Crown Court, had denied stealing the lambs Three animal rights activists have been found guilty of stealing three lambs from the King's Sandringham Estate.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: Throughout a three-day trial, Rosa Sharkey, 26, Sarah Foy, 26, and Rose Patterson, 37, insisted they rescued the animals in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: The members of campaign group Animal Rising also said they believed the King "would have consented to their rescue" due to being an "environmentalist".
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: But the jury of five men and seven women at Norwich Crown Court unanimously found all three guilty of theft.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: They were each sentenced to a 12-month community order of 150 hours of unpaid work, and they must each pay £250 towards prosecution costs.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: Sentencing them, judge Anthony Bate said their actions highlighted "sensitive and important matters of public interest".
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: He added that the defendants were all "intelligent and capable women who can make a valuable contribution to society".
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: The court heard they then took three lambs and put them into a van after they came close, and they were driven off to an unknown animal sanctuary.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: The following day, the women travelled to Windsor Castle, where they attempted to alert authorities to what they called a "rescue" of the lambs.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: They later handed themselves in to Windsor Police Station and were charged with theft.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: Videos of the trio taking the lambs were shared on social media Earlier in the hearing on Thursday, defence barrister Sarah-Jane Ewart, representing Sharkey, insisted the trio had acted "honestly" throughout.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: She highlighted their attempt to alert the authorities at Windsor as an example.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: In the trial, all three defendants detailed how their personal experiences had led them to become involved in animal rights activism, due to concerns about welfare and the environmental impact of agriculture.
sentences.article_title: Activists found guilty of theft of King's lambs

sentences.text: The lambs have never been recovered by the authorities but remained alive and well at an unknown sanctuary, the court heard.

sentences.text: The Conservatives have promised to prevent long-term jobless benefit claimants from spending their welfare payments on alcohol, cigarettes and gambling.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Under the party's proposals, claimants who have been unemployed for more than six months would see their Universal Credit cut by 30% if they have not previously paid enough into the system, despite being able to work.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: This reduced rate would be paid onto a "Back to Work" card, which would not allow cash withdrawals or spending on these items.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The Tories said the proposals were designed to encourage people back into work and cut the soaring welfare bill but Labour branded the scheme "unworkable".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: A Labour Party spokesperson said: "The Conservatives had 14 years to fix our welfare system but they completely failed to make meaningful reforms.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Under the proposals, anyone fit to work would get six months on full benefits to find a job.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Every two years a claimant has previously worked would buy an extra year on the full rate of Universal Credit - but those who have not contributed enough would drop to a new "subsistence allowance", worth 70% of the full rate.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The party said this would protect "those with a strong employment record".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: For example, a 58-year-old who has worked since leaving school but has been made redundant would keep the full allowance up to state pension age.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Claimants who are sick, disabled or already in work would also be exempt, with only those judged capable of work affected.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The Tories said the reduced subsistence allowance would be loaded onto pre-paid card that would not allow cash withdrawals, and would "prevent spending" on alcohol, cigarettes, or gambling.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The party is yet to detail how its proposal would work, but shadow welfare secretary Helen Whately said it would be "a version" of the pre-paid Aspen card issued to asylum seekers living in government-funded accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: These cards cannot be used to make contactless, telephone or internet payments, whilst asylum seekers whose applications have failed cannot withdraw cash.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The Home Office confirmed last year it had tightened the list of permitted retailers where the cards can be used, after reports that some asylum seekers had used the cards to gamble in sites such as slot machine arcades.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Whately said the party would also look to learn from Australia, where certain claimants are issued with debit cards that restrict purchases , external at shops selling alcohol, tobacco products or pornography.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the current system "where someone who can work chooses not to, and earns more benefits than someone in a job" was "unfair".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "The best welfare is a well-paid job.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: So, we will be tough on those who exploit the system because the current system is unfair to workers, taxpayers and those who truly need support," she said.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "Welfare must be a safety net for those who genuinely need it, not a lifestyle choice for those who can't be bothered." However, Helen Barnard, director of policy and research at the anti-poverty charity Trussell, said the proposals were "deeply misguided".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "Universal Credit already falls well short of what people need to afford the essentials like food and heating, forcing people across the UK to the doors of food banks," she said.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "We see people's health being damaged and their ability to find and maintain work undermined by the severe hardship so many are facing." Reform UK's economy spokesman, Robert Jenrick, said the Tories had left record numbers on long-term benefits and the proposals "won't even put a dent" in the welfare bill.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The Conservatives have already pledged to scrap Personal Independence Payment, the main disability benefit in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, for "low-level" mental health conditions to help cut the welfare bill.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The party also wants to make it harder to claim sickness benefits, which it said would mean more people are required to look for work.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Spending on benefits has ballooned in recent years and is forecast to rise to £408.6bn in 2030/31, according to figures from the Department for Work and Pensions.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has insisted he will get the welfare bill down, for example by tackling the number of young people not in education, employment or training, but not through "crude cuts".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Cath Bowie has an audience of around 24,000 followers on Fortnite A 78-year-old Scottish grandmother has been named the world's oldest female Fortnite streamer by Guinness World Records.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: Cath Bowie, who is originally from Moray but now lives in Inverurie, began playing the online shooter in 2017 and now has an audience of more than 24,000 followers.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: She was introduced to the game by her grandson, who was 17 at the time, and says no-one is "ever too old to start gaming".
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: Known on Fortnite her username grumpygran1948, Cath features in the Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition 2027.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: Fortnite is one of the most popular video games in the world, putting up to 100 players against each other in a fight to be the last one standing.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: This video can not be played Gamer gran named world's oldest female Fortnite streamer Cath had tried video games before, but none fully sparked her interest until she discovered Fortnite.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "I was immediately hooked," she said.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: She then bought her own console, but her grandson doubted she would grow a following as a streamer.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: She said: "As a young guy, he just couldn't believe that his grandma would do such a thing and suggested that nobody would join me or watch me.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "Saying that was like a red rag to a bull to me.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: I would show him that I could do it.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "Twenty four thousand followers later and he doesn't mention it.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: I wonder why?" Fortnite is one of the world's most popular online video games Cath says she loves the challenge of the game but also likes chatting to other players Cath said she loves the challenge the game gives her and plays it every day.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: She told the BBC's Radio Scotland Breakfast programme: "It's a lovely, lovely game.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: The one I play is Battle Royale Last Man Standing and you go into it either as a solo, duo or squad.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "You're trying to get the better of your opponents and eliminate them.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "But there's no blood on the scene - you just shoot somebody and they either crawl about until they die or they're just obliterated with the one shot.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: So there isn't any mess - nothing like that." Cath is welcomed into the 2027 Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition Cath said the community of people playing the game was more important than the game itself.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "I play with some wonderful folk - from the UK, quite a few from the USA, from Canada, New Zealand and Australia," she said.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "It's super meeting all these folk.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: The chat we have, it's lovely - I've had folk with me for quite a few years now." Alice Bell, editor of Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition 2027, said: "At Guinness World Records we believe gaming is for everyone.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: "This edition showcases gamers of different generations and cultures from around the world.
sentences.article_title: Meet Grumpygran1948 - Fornite's record breaking streamer

sentences.text: The cost of the whey protein Amarpreet Singh buys has almost tripled since 2020 Amarpreet Singh has been drinking protein shakes since he was 16.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: The 30-year-old, who lives in London and works in banking, started going to the gym at a time when he says protein supplements were mostly associated with bodybuilders.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Fourteen years later, shakes are still part of his routine, but they have become considerably more expensive.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: He says a 4.5kg bag of the whey protein he buys cost around £60 in 2020.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: By last year, the price had gone up to £120, though he managed to get one from eBay for £90.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Now the same bag is £170.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "I was a bit gobsmacked," he says.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Among his gym friends, the rising prices have even been given a nickname – "proteinflation".
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Student Evie says the tub she buys is quite expensive for the size of it Over the years, protein powders and shakes have attracted a much broader customer base, while food manufacturers now offer high-protein versions of everything from bagels to water.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Evie Lewis is a more recent buyer of protein powder.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: The 19-year-old University of Manchester student began using it a few months ago because she felt she wasn't getting enough protein in her diet.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "You hear a lot more about protein now on social media," she says.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: But at £32.99 for a 420g tub, she's feeling the high price and tries to make the product stretch.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "I've been rationing it and using less than what's suggested," she admits.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Max Longman, 32, from Manchester, works in real estate and has been taking protein supplements for 10 years, originally to help him gain weight.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: He now drinks a protein shake every day and says his monthly spending on whey protein has risen from around £45 a year ago to £60 now.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "Loads of foods have protein added to them now.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Up until a few years ago, I'd never heard of high-protein yoghurt, and now I eat it three or four times a week," he says.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Max Longman has been taking protein supplements for 10 years More recently, weight-loss drugs such as Wegovy and Mounjaro have added another source of demand.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: People taking these drugs typically eat less, and are often encouraged to make sure they get enough protein while losing weight to help preserve muscle.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: But that growing appetite for protein is running up against a problem - supply has not kept pace.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: And the result has been a sharp rise in the wholesale price of some key ingredients, and consumers are feeling the squeeze.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: There is no equivalent UK measure, but Expana says the UK market is closely linked to mainland Europe, where some British businesses source their whey protein.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Other dairy proteins have also become more expensive, with another type of whey protein up 60% over the year, while one type of milk protein concentrate was up 80%.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Manufacturers say that increasing production takes time and is costly, as producing high-protein whey requires specialist processing and drying equipment.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: So some are starting to adapt what they make, by changing recipes or looking for cheaper sources of protein.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: Kieran Fisher's company Warrior is launching a product using cheaper sources of protein Warrior, a UK sports nutrition company, is one of those looking for alternatives.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "Our whey protein powder was £12.50 on the shelf last year.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: We've put that up to £17.99 and we're still subsidising that from other aspects of the business," says its founder Kieran Fisher.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: The company is now launching a product using other sources of protein, which Fisher says costs around half as much as whey.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: The effects are also being felt outside the fitness market.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: There are, however, early signs that the market is starting to adjust.

sentences.text: Wholesale prices for high-protein whey have begun to level off over the past couple of months, although they remain much higher than they were a few years ago.

sentences.text: For now though, the higher prices aren't putting off Max.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "It feels like protein is so important now, a lot more than it used to be.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: It's pushed out everywhere," he says.
sentences.article_title: £170 a bag? Protein users squeezed as prices soar

sentences.text: "If you're doing exercise and not taking any, you feel like you wouldn't be recovering properly." But for students like Evie, managing on a much tighter budget, it's a different story.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: We ask New Yorkers to share the smallest amount they'd ask a friend to pay back You pick up the bill for dinner, pay for the taxi home or grab a friend's coffee with the promise they'll pay you back later, but days go by and the money never arrives.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: At what point do you ask them for it again and how small is too small to chase?
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: For some, $5 (£3.70) is worth a reminder, while for others, asking a friend to repay anything under $20 (£15) feels more awkward than simply taking the hit.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: Henry Payne says he's "sent a request for $8.50, but I wouldn't go lower than $8".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: The 21-year-old New Yorker adds that he will chase someone once but "two requests is insane".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "I would rather swallow the $8.50 than send another request." He does admit that he's sometimes the person on the other side of the transaction and can be forgetful himself.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "For everyone that I haven't sent back money to, I just forgot, feel free to double request me." Nouria (left) and Kaz are two students in New York who say money conversations with friends can be very awkward Kaz Jahanbini, 19, says needing to ask to be paid back in the first place can be frustrating.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "If someone bought me something, I'm immediately paying them back.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: So then I'm thinking for them, what's the delay?" His rule for navigating friendship and finances is to "keep your wallet close but your friends closer".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: A recent study , external found that 76% of Gen Z who have fronted money for a group expense, like a trip or event, say they were not fully repaid, and 55% say it created tension or negatively affected a relationship.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: Betsie believes there's a cultural difference between Brits and Americans For British student Betsie Brooke-Taylor, 19, the threshold to ask for money back is a fiver as she says "every little helps".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: She sees a cultural difference between the UK and US and even though "we are all broke, I think Americans are a bit more generous".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: Betsie also thinks technology makes settling small debts easier in the US, where payment apps such as Venmo are widely used.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "In the UK you have to ask for the account number and sort code, and not everyone has that on hand," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: Annika (left) and Hanako feel very differently about confronting a friend who hasn't paid them back For 19-year-old Annika Violet, the amount she would ask back from a friend depends on whether she's consistently paying for them.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "I prefer to do something where I get them this time and they get me next time but if I'm consistently paying and you're not, then I will request the $5." Unlike many, Annika doesn't find money conversations uncomfortable.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "I am so confrontational, I do not find it awkward.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "I've never chased anyone - I'm just sad if I don't get paid back." Annika's advice to those who do struggle to ask is to "be brave and bold".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "If they are going to give you flak about it, maybe it's a sign they are not a good friend." Money expert Laura Pomfret says many people feel embarrassed about asking to be paid back, and Britons in particular can find it awkward.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "We're often very British about asking for money back," she says, suggesting people may be worried about being judged as a "cheapskate".
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: The long nose of the X-59 is designed to damped the plane's sonic boom There's a weird and wonderful jet flying over the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It has the nose of anteater, parts cannibalised from other planes and a cockpit so far back the pilot depends on a camera to see where he's going.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This contraption, the X-59, might just be the future of air travel.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-59's owes its eccentric design to the problem of sonic booms.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The shockwave created by a jet breaking the sound barrier restricted Concorde to flights over the sea and barred it from lucrative routes across the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Now Nasa is working around that problem using the X-59's elongated snout to flatten supersonic booms into tolerable bumps in the background.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In the case of the X-1, flown through the sound barrier in 1947 by the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager, Nasa knew a .50 calibre bullet travelled faster than the speed of sound.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A mere 20 years later the X-15 rocket plane, a cylinder with tiny wings dropped from a B-52 bomber, flew to 6.7 times the speed of sound (4,520 mph) and the edge of space, paving the way for heat-resistant materials vital to the Space Shuttle.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In 1947 the Bell X-1 was the first plane to break the sound barrier Nasa is flying the X-59 in conjunction with community surveys to assess what people think when a supersonic boom is bent by the planes stretched nose and hushed up.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: With its cockpit and ejector seat taken from a T-38 training jet, its landing gear from an F-16 fighter and engine courtesy of the F-18 this jigsaw of an aircraft was assembled by Lockheed Martin for Nasa.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A camera feeding a screen in front of the pilot relies on instantaneous computer processing to get round the lack of forward vision.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It first flew in 2025 and is now breaking the sound barrier over chosen US towns.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But is there still a place for X-plane projects in a world where relatively cheap drones are being rapidly developed - not least in Ukraine's war against Russia .
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Even Nasa considered an uncrewed X-59.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But drones are not always a cheaper option.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Removing the pilot would have added the cost and complication of certifying a robot jet to fly fast over urban areas.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Plus the X-59 had to be big enough to resemble an airliner punching through the sound barrier, which in turn allowed space for a cockpit.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Nasa is no stranger to drone X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48, a scaled down model of an airliner that blends wing and fuselage to create a single lifting body, flew in 2007.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Small was beautiful for the tiny X-48 with its 20ft wingspan as this kept the programme within budget.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "It's likely that future X-planes will be uncrewed," says Coen, before adding the vital caveats "unless the technology we're researching relates to piloting or if crewing it is more cost-effective".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48 was a scaled-down plane to test a blended wing and fuselage Guy Gratton, professor of Aircraft Test and Evaluation at Cranfield University, gets frustrated at the suggestion crewed test planes have had their day.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "There's a belief in certain quarters that drones can do everything.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In Ukraine they've done amazing things with drones, but if you want to carry people you can't take short-cuts." Gratton has tested light aircraft and stresses the importance of a human in the loop.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You lose a huge amount without pilots, you miss lessons a pilot would identify, plus it can take four times as many people on the ground to test a drone." Staff monitoring signals from a drone are an indirect cost that keeps some piloted X-planes relatively affordable.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The Experimental Aircraft Programme tested systems for the Typhoon fighter.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The UK has flown its own technology testbeds and Chris Yeo was in the pilot's seat of one.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The Experimental Aircraft Programme (EAP) flew from Lancashire in 1986 and tried out core systems for the Typhoon fighter.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Yeo acknowledges the EAP's shared heritage with X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "They all research some facet of flight, and demonstrate the design is working correctly.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A lot of people say they can do something, but you only know it works when the design has been tested and certified." Forty years on from Yeo's EAP flights a new UK technology demonstrator is taking shape.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It is, says Tony Godbold who runs the project for BAE Systems, "the X-plane of our generation".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This BAE Systems initiative pulls together 100 UK suppliers including Rolls-Royce to test out ideas that might make it into the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a fighter due to fly in the 2030s.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The technology demonstrator will borrow engines from the existing Typhoon and fly sometime in 2028.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You can model a lot on computers and simulators, but the experience of test pilots is when stuff gets real, we only really learn things when we get their feedback," Godbold admits.

sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Lidl must stop selling Birkenstock copies, including sandals based on the "Arizona" worn here by actor Jason Mamoa Lidl must stop selling copycat versions of Birkenstock's famous sandals in the Netherlands, a Dutch court has ruled.

sentences.text: Lidl must also compensate Birkenstock and pay its legal fees, with the amount to be decided in separate court decisions.

sentences.text: People off sick from work should keep in phone contact with their boss, government-appointed back-to-work expert Sir Charlie Mayfield has said.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: Getting bosses and workers to have a conversation, rather than simply exchanging emails and sicknotes, could help get people back into work, Sir Charlie, who is leading the Keep Britain Working taskforce, said.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: His latest report said health-related economic inactivity was costing Britain around £210bn a year in benefit payments and lost output.

sentences.text: Talking on the phone was just "one piece of the jigsaw" he said on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: But improving communication was also a way to "rehumanise" the workplace and help prevent people dropping out of work altogether, Sir Charlie said.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: Why calling in sick makes you feel guilty The report does not suggest that someone struck down by flu needs to croak through their symptoms over the phone or that bosses need to provide down-the-line sickbed sympathy if an employee is off with food poisoning.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: "I'm not worried about a day here and a day there.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: It is more about longer term issues," Sir Charlie told the BBC's Today Programme.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: But he said Britain was doing a "poor job" of handling sickness in the workplace, leading to more people becoming disengaged and dropping out altogether.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: "I have met so many people who have said to me, 'You know, I was signed off sick and I was off sick for a month, two months, three months, and I had almost no contact with my employer'," Sir Charlie said.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: Around 300,000 people leave work every year with a health condition, much of which is preventable, the report said.
sentences.article_title: Off sick? You need to phone your boss, back-to-work adviser says

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.
