sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company Visit Toledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has branded a ban on fans being allowed to drink alcohol in the stands during men's football matches as "discrimination".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The prime minister told reporters that "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out", as he suggested a change could be trialled.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Laws are in place which prevent drinking in view of the pitch at stadiums for clubs in the top five tiers of men's football in England.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Other sports do not face such a restriction.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) said the "outdated" legislation should be reviewed, but police chiefs have warned against relaxing the law and would like to meet the PM to "explain the challenges".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The legislation was introduced in 1985 by Margaret Thatcher's government for English and Welsh football grounds.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: At the time, then-Home Secretary Leon Brittan said that alcohol was a "major contributory factor in violent and disorderly behaviour" in football grounds.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Burnham is a keen football fan and a season-ticket holder at Premier League team Everton.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Shortly before he became prime minister, he criticised the restriction on football fans as he attended a rugby league game at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium where it was possible for supporters to have a drink in the stands.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Speaking to reporters on his trip to the United Nations in New York, Burnham was asked if it was still his view now he is in Downing Street.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Burnham replied: "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: "And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: There are different ways it could be done.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: It could happen on a trial basis.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: "But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long held view of mine.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently." Government sources have stressed that Burnham was restating an opinion that he has long held, rather than making any sort of policy announcement.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The prime minister's comments are not being seen inside government as an indication that he is looking to change the law in the area.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: A trial or pilot scheme to look at whether a change would be possible is not being ruled out but any wider move would require extensive consultation involving football clubs, fans and the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport - none of which is currently planned.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: A UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) spokesman warned that changes to the law would pose "challenges" to policing and the "safety of staff and fans at football games".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: He said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: "It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games." He added it would be "incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence and meaningful consultation with police practitioners who have the expertise in this area".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: FSA chairman Tom Greatrex said it was "unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match - especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: He said "many clubs" were in favour of a change, adding: "We welcome the prime minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed." A fan-led review of football governance in 2021 called for the law to be re-examined.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The rules have been relaxed this season with all Women's Super League (WSL) clubs allowed to offer alcohol to supporters in the stands following two seasons of successful trials.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The law is more restrictive in Scotland, where the general sale of alcohol has been prohibited in Scottish football stadiums since 1981, but trial sales have been taking place recently and fans can now buy alcohol at Hampden Park games .
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: This video can not be played The UK is reviewing its deal to hand over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, the defence secretary has said.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Wes Streeting confirmed the deal was being looked at again after US President Donald Trump called it "terrible" at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: The original agreement would see the UK cede sovereignty of the territory to Mauritius and pay an average of £101m ($136m) per year to lease back a joint UK-US military base there, prized for its strategic location in the Indian Ocean.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: In April the deal, agreed under Sir Keir Starmer, was paused indefinitely because Trump pulled his support.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Streeting said "we have to" review the deal "because the United States doesn't support it".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: "What President Trump said yesterday wasn't new but I think it does provide absolute clarity that his position on this Chagos deal as currently drafted is not changing," he told BBC Breakfast.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: "So we have to do more work with our American allies, with President Trump and his administration, to get the deal to a place where he can support it." Streeting said the focus now would be to secure a long-term certainty for the base on Diego Garcia, the Chagos archipelago's largest island.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: He said it had been the view of every UK prime minister since Boris Johnson that an ongoing legal process - as Mauritius argues it was illegally forced to give away the islands in 1965 to gain independence - risks the security of the base.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: During Trump's first face-to-face meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the UN General Assembly in New York, the US president criticised the "terrible deal" and said the UK was "going to be looking" at it.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: He later told broadcasters he has "inherited the situation and we need a resolution".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Burnham added: "It's critical to safeguard the future of the base, and that matters to us for security reasons, but also clearly to the United States as well.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: The "review" is not expected to constitute a formal process operating to a specific timeframe.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Government sources are insisting that Burnham and Streeting's comments do not represent a major shift from the previous position, which was that any deal would require American support.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: However Streeting's comments were notable for their explicit acknowledgement that without changes the deal is not going to attract Trump's support.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Prior to the pause in April, the UK and Mauritius had signed an agreement in May 2025 and a final draft of the bill to hand over sovereignty of the islands had not passed Parliament.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Under the terms of the deal agreed in 2025 , Britain would hand sovereignty over the archipelago to Mauritius but lease back the Diego Garcia base for 99 years, which the UK government said would be a net overall cost of £3.4bn.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: However, Sir Keir, who was then prime minister, came under heavy criticism from opponents who said the real cost of the deal could amount to £35bn, adjusting for inflation, and risked allowing China to establish a presence on the archipelago.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Trump, who originally backed the deal, has been a frequent critic of the move, previously branding it a "a blight on our great ally" and an "act of total weakness".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Reacting to the review, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called on Burnham to "just scrap this terrible deal".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "The Chagos deal is dead.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Thank God." In 2019, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) gave an advisory opinion that Britain's separation of the Chagos Islands from Mauritius was unlawful and stated the UK must end its administration as rapidly as possible.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: While non-binding, the ICJ advisory opinion - which was endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly - emboldened Mauritian assertions of sovereignty and led to the UK opening negotiations in 2022 .
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Streeting told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Wednesday that no money would be handed over to Mauritius "at this stage" while officials review the deal.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Describing the Diego Garcia base as "one of the most sensitive and valuable national security assets", he said work was underway to find a deal "that maybe not everyone loves, but everyone can live with".

sentences.text: Camden Town is at the heart of Holborn and St Pancras constituency On 8 October, voters in the Holborn and St Pancras constituency will choose their next MP.
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: A win in this seat, which has returned Labour MPs for decades, would be a feather in the cap of the Green Party after Sir Keir Starmer stood down from the House of Commons at the start of September, shortly after leaving office as prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: Labour are confident of holding on, but the Greens also have high hopes of winning their first London seat - and there are 13 other candidates in the mix all hoping to take this central London constituency.
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: BBC London spoke to five of the leading candidates.
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: Zack Polanski says people in the constituency want change Zack Polanski, the Green Party candidate, told BBC London he was "feeling confident or I wouldn't have put my hat in the ring in the first place, but I'm not complacent".
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: He said he would "work with the Labour government constructively on the things we agree with".
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: "People are telling me over and over again they can't afford the cost of housing, they need more council housing.
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: "Renters who need rent control, leaseholders who need justice for leaseholders.
sentences.article_title: Greens aim for first London MP in Holborn race

sentences.text: The government said they'd end this feudal system of leasehold and then haven't taken the action." When asked about the last time he ran in Camden, as a Liberal Democrat candidate for the council, he said: "I think in politics we need less politicians who treat political parties like football teams.

sentences.text: "I want to make sure that particularly with housing, for instance, it's an issue.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Key moments from Andy Burnham's first UN speech The UK will set up a new centre to "stem the poisonous tide" of disinformation, including from Russia, and lead efforts to establish global safety standards for artificial intelligence, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said.

sentences.text: In his first major international speech at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, Burnham warned Russian agencies are using "every means at their disposal", including bots and fake websites, to "spread lies and disinformation".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The prime minister noted AI will "multiply" existing threats, and pitched the UK as an "honest broker" on the technology.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Fears about AI have grown after industry insiders recently warned it could threaten humanity.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: In Burnham's speech, he accused Russia of running a disinformation campaign.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: "The Kremlin spends around £1.3bn each year on manipulating information," Burnham told the UN General Assembly.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: "They've used bots and fake websites, falsified newspaper articles, forged the branding of 28 British organisations, including universities and the BBC.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: "We're talking about an insidious campaign that reaches into people's homes and twists what they feel about their own country and community – creating a narrative of decline, stoking division and sowing despair.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: "On top of that we have seen cyber-attacks on our companies and institutions.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: And we know that AI will multiply the threat."' He also referenced the 2019 UK general election, in which the government previously said Russia almost certainly sought to interfere.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: To counter this, Burnham announced a new National Centre for Information Defence to detect and disrupt AI-enabled disinformation campaigns by hostile states.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The centre will work alongside intelligence agencies, government departments, law enforcement and social media to bring together expertise to combat "information warfare".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: There was no immediate comment from Russia, a representative of which was sitting in the room listening to Burnham.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: When the UK government put out a report in 2020 about Russian activity in the UK, including in elections, Moscow described the allegations as "Russophobia".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Addressing a forum about disinformation in Moscow on Tuesday, before the prime minister's speech, Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov accused Western media of embracing "anti-Russian cliches and fantasies".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage accused Burnham's government of using the "excuse" of real bot accounts from Russia and India interfering in politics to "clamp down on free speech".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: This video can not be played Burnham: UK to fight Russian disinformation Chris Mason: From inside the room, how Burnham survived first Trump meeting Before becoming prime minister, Burnham had said relatively little about how AI should be regulated.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Since taking power in July, Burnham's government has stressed the need for international cooperation to combat the risks, as well as harness the potential benefits of the technology, warning that further regulation and legislation may be needed.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: In his speech, Burnham described the most advanced "Frontier AI" as "one of the most significant challenges and opportunities of our age".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: He told world leaders AI would be "key to economic growth" but also a "multiplier of risk".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The prime minister added: "We've all heard the warnings – which we must heed.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: I know how worried people are.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: So we have to rise to this moment." Burnham said the "UK has a unique position as an honest broker", with close ties to the US and the European Union.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: He also highlighted the UK's "world-leading" AI Security Institute,  which was established under Conservative Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and tests major AI models to improve their safety before they are released publicly.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: He pledged to put AI "at the heart of the UK's G20 Presidency next year", when leaders of the world's biggest economies will gather in Manchester.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Chris Mason: How Burnham survived his first Trump meeting Hear from the BBC's political editor Chris Mason, who is travelling with the prime minister and was in the room when they first met.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham said the UK would work towards agreeing a set of global principles and standards to ensure transparency, access to AI models, and that development happens safely.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: He added that this would "bring together welcome initiatives from others", such as a proposal from Norway this week.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The declaration - which has the support of more than 20 countries, including Germany, Canada and Ireland - calls for AI to remain under human control and for mandatory pre-release testing of frontier models.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: However, it has not been signed by the US and China, which dominate AI development, or the UK.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Former cabinet minister Darren Jones, who served as chief secretary to Burnham's predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, called on the prime minister to sign the declaration and offer to broker an agreement with the US on its implementation.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: He argued there "should be a landing zone to agree mandatory testing", without undermining competitive advantage between companies and nations.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The UK AI Security Institute's testing of models is currently on a voluntary basis and AI company Anthropic reportedly refused to submit its latest model for testing.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Downing Street said officials had made clear in recent discussions with AI leaders that the government expects "full and total visibility of model developments".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The prime minister has acknowledged that while developers have made significant commitments on transparency, nothing is off the table to keep the public safe, including legislation.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats and the Green Party have been putting pressure on the government to take further action on AI safety.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: However, any international efforts to regulate AI would need the cooperation of the US and China.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: In his own address earlier, US President Donald Trump rejected "any attempt to construct a globalist scheme" to control AI.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: "We're going to encourage it, not rein it in," he told the UN General Assembly.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Trump has previously dismissed warnings of AI destroying humanity as "a hoax".
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Burnham and Trump met for the first time in person on Tuesday, although Downing Street's statement on the meeting did not mention that they discussed AI.
sentences.article_title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the government has announced a new AI and Autonomy partnership between the UK and US, focused on protecting critical national infrastructure using AI tech.

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After divorcing her husband and coming out as lesbian, Mindy co-founded a lesbian commune in Hull before moving to Manchester On one occasion, while Mindy was in hospital after a stroke, a nurse referred to Linda as Mindy's husband.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She said it was not only "insulting", but made her consider what sort of training the staff might have had.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Spotlight on Ageing report says these sort of experiences can also have an impact on the support people receive.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Wilkinson, research and analysis manager at the Centre for Ageing Better, says after a "lifetime of homophobia and transphobia", older LGBTQ+ people now face the "additional, and overlapping, challenge of ageism".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report , external says older LGBTQ+ people are less likely to have children - someone born in 1950 would have been in their 50s by the time same-sex couples could legally adopt - and that they are more likely to be estranged from their families when compared to their heterosexual counterparts.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report also found more than half of gay and bisexual men aged 65 and above live alone, compared with less than a quarter of heterosexual men.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Bisexual women aged 50 to 64 are twice as likely as their heterosexual peers to live alone.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: It also suggests that only half of gay and bisexual men aged 50 and above definitely agree they would have someone to help them if they needed, 14 percentage points lower than heterosexual men of the same age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman Goodman, 75, came out as bisexual in his late 60s after the death of his wife Marilyn.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The couple never had children, and Norman now has no immediate family nearby to help him with things like hospital visits or housework.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: He says his support system comes in the form of his partner Tony, and a group of friends and neighbours he refers to as his "chosen family".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I'm lucky, I've got great friends and great neighbours, and I know I can knock on somebody's door day or night and I could get help," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman came out as bisexual when he was in his 60s and says he relies on "chosen family" to support him But despite having their support while he's relatively independent, Norman says he worries about the prospect of facing discrimination if he needs more formal care as he ages.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "Hopefully I will maintain and look after myself the best I can, but I've heard horror stories of gay people in nursing homes being treated terribly," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think nurses, doctors, carers should all be trained on how to look after LGBT people." It's the reason behind schemes like Manchester's Kindred House, which are not unusual in other parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There are similar projects in Spain, Sweden, Germany, the US and Canada, but in the UK they are few and far between.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: In 2021, the UK's first LGBTQ+ retirement community, Tonic, opened in London with 19 apartments for affordable rental or shared ownership.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The scheme attracted so much attention, later this year it is set to feature in a Netflix documentary telling the story of one of its first residents, Chek Min-Ong.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After 43 years together, Min, 77, and his late partner Tim, had discussed their plans for a future where one of them would live alone, as Tim's health deteriorated.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Min and his late partner Tim wanted to make sure they lived somewhere supportive when one of them passed away "Tim and I have always had this very open discussion, we wanted to know, when one of us is not here anymore, the other person will have a community and feel safe," Min says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: When Tim died five months after moving into Tonic, Min says his new-found community rallied around him.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It is what [Tim and I] always wanted, that we'd never have to explain ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "We'd never have to face a question and feel guilty about not telling the full story, or having to lie.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "You're just here, being yourself." While schemes like Kindred House and Tonic are welcomed by Mindy, Norman and Min, the Spotlight on Ageing report warns that, because the older LGBTQ+ population is growing, the demand for specialist services is expected to outstrip supply.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the number of over-50s identifying as lesbian, gay or bisexual in the UK increased by around a third - from roughly 340,000 to almost 460,000.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There was a 4% rise in the number of heterosexual people aged 50 and above in the same period.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: These numbers are projected to continue to increase as the relatively larger younger generations of people identifying as LGBTQ+ age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston warns that without more schemes like Kindred House, and more training and awareness for those in other care settings, the ageing population may struggle to get proper support.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: For Mindy, who is part of a steering group advising on the plans, knowing there may be more options available in the future is reassuring.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's important that you can go, that you think, 'You know what, I could live there because I know the staffing, the ethics, the rules, everything about the place has been put together from an LGBTQ+ focus,'" she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "That's what we've been doing and it's something I'm really proud of being a part of."

sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The BBC has approached Garmin for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Jess's sleep scores weren't matching how she actually felt Dr Neil Stanley, sleep expert and author of the book How to Sleep Well, argues that gamifying sleep is creating more disordered sleeping.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures." He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Though commercial trackers now are a bit more sophisticated, they work in much the same way - by measuring your movement - and have the same limitations, he says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," Stanley adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "Unless you're measuring the brain's activities, you're not measuring sleep." Keeping your bedroom cool, dark and quiet - within reason.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That doesn't mean it needs to be pitch black, exactly 16C or totally silent," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It should be coolish, darkish and quietish." Seeing bright light in the morning, which is good for regulating your circadian rhythm - that is, your body's natural clock.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Doing light exercise, and eating a "healthy, Mediterranean-style diet with plenty of plant variability".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Above all, keeping it simple - "anything else, you don't need it".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts
