sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Periods of hot weather can affect anyone, but some people run a greater risk of serious harm.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This, combined with the lowered blood pressure, can lead to heat exhaustion.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Symptoms include: If blood pressure drops too far, the risk of heart attacks rises.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: How does sunscreen work, and how much do you need to use?
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Staying safe in water when the weather's hot Our bodies strive to keep a core temperature of about 37C whether we are in a snowstorm or a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: That is the temperature at which our bodies have evolved to work.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: But as the weather gets hotter, it is harder for the body to keep its core temperature down.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: It opens more blood vessels near the skin to lose heat to our surroundings and starts sweating.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the sweat evaporates, it dramatically increases the heat lost from the skin.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: No one - especially babies, young children and animals - should ever be left in a locked vehicle.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Hot weather: How to sleep in the heat Six ways to keep your home and yourself cool in hot weather When is it too hot to walk your dog?

sentences.text: If you see someone you think has heat exhaustion , the NHS says you should: , external move them to a cool place get them to lie down and raise their feet slightly get them to drink plenty of water - sports or rehydration drinks are also OK cool their skin - spray or sponge them with cool water and fan them.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Cold packs around the armpits or neck are also good If they can be cooled down within half an hour, then heat exhaustion is not normally serious.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, if they do not recover within 30 minutes, then they are at risk of heatstroke .
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This is a medical emergency and you should call 999 immediately.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People with heatstroke may stop sweating even though they are too hot.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Their temperature could go over 40C and they might have seizures or lose consciousness.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: What to do if you think someone has heat exhaustion or heatstroke People who are older or have some long-term conditions - such as heart disease -  are sometimes less able to cope with the strain heat puts on the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diabetes can make the body lose water more quickly and some complications of the disease can alter blood vessels and the ability to sweat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Children and those who are less mobile may also be more vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Brain diseases, such as dementia, can also leave people unaware of the heat or unable to do anything about it.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People who are homeless will also be more exposed to the sun.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Those living in top-floor flats will also face higher temperatures.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Yes - but the NHS says people should keep taking their medication as normal, and focus on staying cool and hydrated.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diuretics - sometimes called "water pills" - increase the amount of water the body expels.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: They are taken widely, including for heart failure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: In high temperatures, they increase the dangers of dehydration and imbalances in key minerals in the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Antihypertensives - which lower blood pressure - can combine with the blood vessels that are dilating to cope with the heat and cause dangerous drops in blood pressure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Some drugs for people with epilepsy and Parkinson's can block sweating and make it harder for the body to cool itself.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Other drugs such as lithium or statins can become more concentrated and problematic in the blood if there is too much fluid loss.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: During 2022 - which saw the highest recorded temperature in England at 40.3C - there were an estimated 2,985 so-called "excess deaths" as a result of the heat , external , the most recorded in any given year.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: There were an estimated 1,311 heat-associated deaths , external during summer 2024, and an estimated 1,504 , external during summer 2025.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Most heat-related excess deaths are due to heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The higher death rate starts to kick in once the thermometer passes 25C-26C.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, evidence suggests the deaths tend to be caused by higher temperatures in spring or early summer rather than during "peak summer".
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This could be because we start to change our day-to-day behaviour as summer progresses and we get more used to dealing with the heat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The evidence from previous heatwaves is the increase in deaths happens very quickly - within the first 24 hours of a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Women in Wolverhampton will be able to collect a sample from home and send it off to be tested for HPV Women in Wolverhampton who have not attended cervical screening appointments are to be offered home testing for human papillomavirus (HPV).

sentences.text: The NHS is rolling out the self-testing kits to increase screening numbers, with data suggesting about a third of women are not up to date with appointments.
sentences.article_title: At-home cervical screenings to roll out in city

sentences.text: HPV is a common virus and some high-risk types can cause changes to cells in the cervix, which can develop into cervical cancer.
sentences.article_title: At-home cervical screenings to roll out in city

sentences.text: Eligible women will be able to order a free self-testing kit online through the NHS app.
sentences.article_title: At-home cervical screenings to roll out in city

sentences.text: The kit contains a swab which is used to collect a sample at home before it is posted off for testing free of charge.
sentences.article_title: At-home cervical screenings to roll out in city

sentences.text: If high-risk HPV is detected, the person will be invited to book a follow-up appointment at their GP surgery or a sexual health clinic.
sentences.article_title: At-home cervical screenings to roll out in city

sentences.text: The HPV self-testing scheme is being introduced in phases across England, initially targeting women aged 30 to 65 who have not attended cervical screening after previous invitations.

sentences.text: A common symptom of the menopause is a hot flush Partners of women going through the menopause are being invited to experience one of the symptoms at a forthcoming support event.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: At the Menopaus'ull Support Network event in Hull next month, health group Over The Bloody Moon will be taking one of its MenoVests, allowing people to experience a hot flush – one of the symptoms of the menopause.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Sarah Weichardt, who co-manages the project, said: "We're particularly interested in getting men along to come and experience the MenoVest, just so that they can understand what women go through." The event will be at Princes Quay shopping centre on 17 October, from 10:30 until 14:30 BST.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "It's not just a hot flush, it's what the hot flush brings with it," said Weichardt.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "So it could be panic, it could be anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: It's experiencing it all at the same time." She said she hoped the vest would give people a "better understanding of what women are going through".
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "The more people we can get to experience it, the better," she added.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: The menopause describes the end of a woman's reproductive years, and often happens at about the age of 50.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: The period leading up to this is called the perimenopause, which is when many women notice their periods becoming unpredictable.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Other symptoms can include mood shifts, difficulty sleeping, and discomfort during sex.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Weichardt said her organisation had a banner with nearly 40 symptoms on it.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Many women "don't necessarily know that they're going into the menopause or they're perimenopausal" until they see the banner – and then they sometimes have a "lightbulb moment", she said.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Once women have "accepted it and are happy" they are menopausal or peri-menopausal, they can seek the support they need, she added.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: There is also a Menopaus'ull Support Network event in Beverley on 10 October between 10:30 and 13:30 BST at the Toll Gavel Church.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Martine Barons who began lifting weights during lockdown is now a three-time world champion A 65-year-old grandmother has become a three-time world champion powerlifter after only starting the sport two and a half years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Martine Barons, from Stratford-upon-Avon, said she began lifting weights during lockdown after listening to a seminar that said women going through menopause should run less and lift more.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Her colleague at the University of Warwick, who is also a personal trainer, then showed Barons how to deadlift, and spotted her potential.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons is now nicknamed The Deadlifting Grandma.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: On Monday, she won at the AWPC World Powerlifting Championships in the 65 to 85 age group, becoming a three-time world champion, after starting out entering competitions just for fun.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said she has seen a "huge change" in her physique and capabilities "I have seen such a huge change in my own physique and my capabilities – I am sure that my body is at least 20 years younger," she told BBC CWR.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "When they invited me to the British and European Championships, I thought, 'Well I have been invited it would be rude not to go', but who thought it would lead to this?
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said her journey, down to hard work and dedication over the past couple of years, has been "so exciting".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "I have learnt so much, I have met people all around the world, and it has been delightful," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: For women who want to get fit and improve their strength, Baron said there were lots of options, one route is to join a gym and develop a tailored programme with a coach.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Alternatively, Baron said those who prefer more privacy could "start really gently at home with some resistance bands and a programme".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: She added her powerlifting has led to having more capability on a day-to-day basis, along with now being able to touch her toes first thing in the morning.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "If I need to move furniture at home, I can do that, I can toss my grandchildren in the air, I can play games with them," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "My posture is better and I just feel more capable and more confident in everyday life".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The centre said schools are legally required to teach pupils about FGM and the law surrounding it as part of relationships and sex education.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "If I knew I could seek help I would not have waited until I was expecting... because I did suffer a lot before." If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Powell told LBC earlier this month that she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT said the results of a recent survey of its members suggested that the majority who responded felt that inspections had worsened in the past 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The union is now calling for inspections to pause to allow for a "fundamental review of how inspection works", drawing on examples from other nations.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: In Wales, the inspectorate Estyn has removed judgements such as "excellent" and "good" from its reports, instead summarising findings by highlighting a school's strengths and areas for improvement.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: They agreed to some but not all of the recommendations made by MPs after an inquiry into student loans, and did not say whether they would reverse a freeze to the repayment threshold for some graduates.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The inquiry found the way loans had been presented to teenagers amounted to mis-selling , after the BBC revealed the Department for Education (DfE) had compared repayments to £30-a-month phone contracts.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year.

sentences.text: The loans are written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at £29,385 for three years in England.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: English pupils have pulled ahead of the rest of the UK in international reading, maths and science tests, new data suggests, with Scotland and Wales falling further behind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The latest Pisa report, which is published every three years, also warned of a worldwide decline in teenagers' reading skills.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Teenagers were losing the skills that "matter most in the age of AI", such as being able to critically evaluate information from different sources, it said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The share of "hasty readers", who rush through texts to give quick, incorrect answers, has almost doubled between 2018 and 2025.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The report warned the fall was greatest in those from "relatively well off" families.

sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.

sentences.text: El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office What is El Niño and why could it mean record temperatures?
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Trade winds that typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean can weaken or even reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Heat is then released from the ocean into the atmosphere which can boost global temperatures and drive changes in weather patterns around the world.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Forecasters track the development of El Niño by watching temperatures in a key region of the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: When these are consistently 0.5C above normal, an El Niño is declared.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: There are different ways of measuring the strength of El Niño, however.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The records that have now been broken relate to daily measurements of sea surface temperature compared with the long term historical average.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This is called the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Many scientists - including forecasters in the USA and Australia - also consider an alternative measure known as the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This measures how warm the key El Niño region is relative to the rest of the tropical oceans, meaning it takes into account the background warming caused by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: By the RONI index the current El Niño is not yet a record-breaker - but it is likely that more announcements will follow in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Adam Scaife, Head of Long Range Prediction at the Met Office, said: "We have been signalling for months that the developing El Niño will be an unprecedented event.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: "The fact that it has already exceeded previous records – with several weeks to go before it peaks later this year – shows the enormity of this El Niño." Every El Niño is different, therefore impacts on global weather patterns are not guaranteed.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: And the unprecedented strength of this El Niño does not necessarily mean it will have unprecedented impacts on the weather.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Scaife said: "Scientists are still assessing whether the impacts will be in proportion to its magnitude, but we are already seeing expected effects worldwide." El Niño increases the odds of storms and floods in some regions and of drought and wildfires in others.

sentences.text: The winter of 2015 and 2016, which coincided with a very strong El Niño, brought a succession of major storms delivering what experts at the time described as the most extreme flooding on record.

sentences.text: Thousands of people are dead or missing after massive floods and landslides tore through the Nepal-Tibet border last month Nepal plans to use a new study linking climate change to the deadly floods last month as the basis of a financial request from a United Nations fund.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The BBC understands that Nepal hopes to claim around $20m (£15m) from the UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, which helps countries affected by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Around 1,400 people have died in the disaster while 6,150 people remain missing in Nepal as of Wednesday, according official data.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The study by research group World Weather Attribution, published on Thursday, says climate change was a likely contributing factor in the avalanche of rock and ice that unleashed devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border last month.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: There was "absolutely no doubt that human-induced climate change played a role here in the preconditioning of the disaster", said Dr Friederike Otto, an Imperial College London climatologist who co-authored the study.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Massive floods and landslides swept through border towns and villages in Nepal and Tibet, wiping out thousands of houses, destroying energy infrastructure and leaving thousands dead or missing.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Scientists say the floods were caused by a collapse of rock wall and glacier ice near the peak of Langtang Lirung, a mountain on Nepal's side of the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The study said the disaster was the result of a "compound event" caused by rising temperatures, thinning glaciers, thawing permafrost and pre-existing geological weaknesses According to the study, July and August temperatures in the area were around 1.5C (2.7F) warmer "due to human influence on the climate".
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Meanwhile, glaciers in the region had also been thinning by about half a metre (1.6ft) a year, which could weaken existing fractures and increase instability.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Heavy snowfall last October and November also added to a large amount of meltwater early this year.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Climate change, while not the only cause of the disaster, was a "destabilising factor acting on a pre-existing geological predisposition", the study said.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: In the wake of the floods, Nepal's leaders have said the country needs around $5bn (£3.7bn) to rebuild itself.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, which came into operation last year, requires countries to submit evidence proving that the losses they faced were caused by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Nepali officials had been preparing satellite and drone images, as well as preliminary reports, to back up its request to the fund.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: But the World Weather Attribution report is now the strongest evidence for their claim that climate change was a significant factor in the collapse of rock and ice at  Langtang Lirung, authorities say.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The report "will be the main basis of our claim as it has detailed what role climate has played in this disaster," said Maheshwar Dhakal, spokesperson for Nepal's Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: What caused the Nepal-Tibet flash floods?
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Nepali authorities have called for global efforts to tackle climate change, saying the country is one of the lowest contributors to greenhouse emissions yet one of the most vulnerable places to the effects of global warming.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: In his first foreign trip as Nepali Prime Minister, Balendra Shah is set to appear at United Nations General Assembly in New York next week to talk about the recent disaster and climate justice.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: "Nepal has repeatedly used the term 'compensation' to describe much-needed recovery funds," said Danya Liu, a climate adaptation specialist at BloombergNEF.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Nearly 120 countries have already submitted claims to the UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, with requests totalling at nearly $3bn (£2.2bn).
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: But the fund reportedly has just less than $400m (£300m) allotted for disbursement.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Nepalese officials have said that while they have garnered wider support from some countries to disburse funds to Nepal rapidly, other countries have stressed the need to follow rules and procedures.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Officials responsible for the UN fund are scheduled to meet in December to decide which requests would be accepted - and whether it would make an urgent decision for Nepal.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The study has not been published in a peer-reviewed journal.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: According to the World Weather Attribution website, its studies all use the same peer-reviewed method in analysing extreme weather events.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Its findings build on what other experts had suggested in the immediate aftermath of the disaster.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Some had previously told the BBC that rising temperatures in the Himalayas was a likely factor in the rock-ice avalanche.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Dr Simon Cook, a glacier expert with the University of Dundee, told the BBC last month that while it was hard to attribute any single event to climate change, "climate warming ultimately destabilises these high mountain environments".
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Cook also told the BBC on Thursday that the World Weather Attribution report was a "very worthwhile study" about the underlying causes of the recent disaster.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: And while it provides "some strong evidence that climate change was a key factor", he said "we are not yet at a point of being able to say exactly how this happened".

sentences.text: The FBI is investigating a claim by a cyber-crime group that it has stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The group, Shiny Hunters, says it has every agent's name, role, badge number and personal details including home address, phone numbers and spouse information.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: Professor Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, said - if confirmed - it was "as serious as it gets when it comes to data breaches." In a statement posted on X, the FBI said it was aware of the claim and the agency was  "actively and aggressively investigating the matter".
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The criminals claim to have breached the FBI's servers on Monday night and began contacting reporters on Tuesday sharing samples and screenshots of the stolen data.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The BBC has seen a small portion of the data, which appears to be genuine.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: According to Reuters, some of the data contains details about officials' ​job assignments, including sensitive work against Chinese spies, Russian intelligence and drug cartels.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: ShinyHunters is an international collective of hackers, believed to have originally started in France.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: It has been behind a number of high-profile breaches including on Rockstar Games in April and a highly disruptive hack on education platform Canvas in May.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The group claims to have found a vulnerability in the Oracle cloud storage system used by the FBI to breach multiple systems including FBIJOBS, FBI BEAST, which does background checks on employees and applicants, FBI MedLink, which holds agent's medical records and FBI BICS, which holds investigation information.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: In its message on the dark web, the group said it did not hack the FBI system for money.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: Instead, the cyber-criminals are asking the agency to retract an advisory that it issued in May about the gang, saying it was "offended" by its characterisation.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: That FBI's public service announcement , external described ShinyHunters as "threat actors" who often "use their real or exaggerated claims of access to sensitive or personal information to prompt payment from victims".
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "They target major companies across tech, finance, and retail, often stealing millions of customer records at once," the advisory said.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: ShinyHunters said it would give the bureau one week to correct or remove what it says are false allegations or they would publish the full databases.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The FBI did not respond to multiple requests for comment from the BBC.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: In its statement on X, the agency said it was trying to determine whether or not the hackers had breached its systems or a third party.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "We are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk," the post said.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: In a statement to the BBC, a cyber-security expert said it was a "retaliation attack", which demonstrated that "no organisation is safe from the group".
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "The group clearly wants to control the narrative around their activities, ensuring nothing is said that could dent their reputation," said William Wright of Closed Door Security.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: Meanwhile Andrew Brandt of cyber-security firm Huntress said it may provoke the FBI to track down and prosecute members of the hacking group.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "ShinyHunters must feel pretty confident they won't get caught to threaten a government agency like this," he said.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: This video can not be played "Good to have choice": Australians on opting-out of social media algorithms The US has criticised Australia's proposal to give users the ability to opt out of social media algorithms, saying it amounts to "censorship of protected speech".
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: Under Australia's draft digital duty of care laws, tech firms risk hefty fines if they fail to give users the option to turn off algorithms in a bid to protect them from harmful content.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: In a rare submission to the proposed laws, the US embassy in Canberra said it had "serious concerns" and allowing the government to "enforce vague definitions of 'harm'" would lead to "viewpoint-based censorship".
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the legislation was not about giving governments control but giving it back to individuals.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: "We ask that Australia clarify how exactly 'harm' and 'risks' shall be determined... ensuring these definitions do not encroach on protected speech," the US said in its submission.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: The US also claimed that the proposed laws may risk "reducing the reach of independent journalists or other voices whose content touches on sensitive or controversial topics" if tech firms had to "pre-emptively demote" them.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: An opt-out option would "allow regulators to impose rigid, one-size-fits-all platform design requirements" on tech firms and this could affect users outside of Australia, it said.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: Another worry was that the proposed laws could affect Australia's "reputation as a jurisdiction that enables innovation," the submission said.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: The criticism comes during Albanese's visit to the US to speak at the UN's General Assembly about his government's tech policies.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: On Tuesday, local time in New York, Albanese responded to the criticism and claims of the proposed laws being government overreach.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: "It's not about giving government control," he told the media in New York.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: This latest move by Australia to protect its online users from harm comes less than a year after the country introduced a social media ban for children under 16 last December.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: Australians will be able to switch off social media algorithms under planned legislation Australia has banned social media for kids under 16.

sentences.text: The regulator said in May that Pornhub started using a new age verification process for some users, which relied on a third party, Apple.

sentences.text: It said it had concerns that Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing" before implementing this new process, and so it "may not be highly effective" at preventing children from seeing pornography.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: In a lengthy statement given to the BBC, Aylo strongly defended its system for age verification while stressing it would cooperate fully with the investigation.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA), sites that host pornographic material must use highly effective age assurance to ensure users are over 18, but it leaves it up to the service to decide the method of age-checking it will use.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Ofcom says as part of its investigation it will consider how Aylo implements its age verification processes and whether it conducted the "necessary due diligence" before it was implemented.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: It will not investigate how Apple operates its age checks.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: George Lusty, Ofcom's Director of Enforcement, said: "Online age checks are a vital protection to prevent children from encountering inappropriate or harmful material, including pornography.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: "We expect tech firms to ensure age checks are highly effective before introducing them.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Anything less could leave children at risk." But Aylo argues that, having experimented in multiple markets with multiple age-check methods, Apple's system "provides significantly stronger protection than any other age assurance method currently available in the UK market".
