sentences.text: Last season, the club's data department projected they would be there or thereabouts when it came to the title race, but their metrics indicated Arsenal were favourites to be champions.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: This time around, City prefer to keep their projections under wraps - but five wins from five Premier League games have prompted predictions from supporters and pundits they will again be the Gunners' closest challengers.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: City's devotion to data is at the heart of their efforts to close the gap on Arsenal and BBC Sport has been given unprecedent access to the inner workings of the club's metrics machine as we uncover some of the secrets guiding their work - particularly regarding player recruitment and sales.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Their work is a sign of the times in the Premier League, with clubs across the top flight and beyond increasingly using data for transfers and monitoring their teams' performance.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: At City, one of the fundamental aims is to reduce risk of any market transaction, be it a purchase or a sale.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: City grade players based on: The system they play in at their current club and how the manager is asking him and the team to play.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Once those four aspects are observed, City's aim is to understand not just how good the player is but how good he could become at the Etihad.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Since winning the Treble in 2023 , City's squad has undergone a vast overhaul using this approach.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Only four players from that historic campaign remain.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: It is crucial to stress, however, that while data has made an indefinite impact on how City operate in the transfer market, the work of traditional scouts continues to be the primary gauge of whether they decide to move for a player.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: "Data plays a role in our decision-making, but it is just one part of the overall picture," City sporting director Hugo Viana told BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: "We know data cannot tell us everything about a player.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: It cannot fully show a person's character, mentality or behaviour.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: "That is why we study data insights but focus on the expertise of our scouts and other specialists." The prominence of data, however, has grown significantly behind the scenes at the Etihad.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Here BBC Sport can take you to the core of some of City's key transfer calls from their extensive three-year squad revamp  - including the £116m signing of Elliot Anderson.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The starting point for any new signing is City's database of 650,000 footballers from around the world.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The next step is the brief: what sort of player is the club wanting to recruit.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: This usually starts with a position, though that process isn't as simple as it sounds.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: City, for example, categorise their full-backs into three types: those who are defensive, those who come inside, and those who play high and wide.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Once the club's data departments have the brief, filters that grade a player's overall ability are applied to whittle down the 650,000-man database to 20-50 names.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Juventus full-back Andrea Cambiaso is one player who has been on City's radar after the data highlighted him, particularly his ability to coming inside to build play in midfield.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: That he is comfortable with both feet rated highly on the data, too.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: In accordance with the data and the scouting reports it was decided the club would not proceed with their interest in Cambiaso in the previous window, but City's approach is likely to mean he will continue to be monitored.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The longlist of 20-50 names is cross-referenced with the scouting longlist.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Generally there is a significant overlap between the players identified by data and the ones already on scouts' radar.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: From there, further, more refined metrics are applied to rank and prioritise the longlist.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Scouts will then complete further diligence on the players to reduce the list to a maximum of about six players.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: At this point, the club will complete deeper dives into the remaining players, including diligence on their injury record, athletic performance and behavioural habits.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The information is then collated into individual reports called acquisition packs which contain all the key metrics used to inform the decision on a player.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: This includes a 'radar chart', which rates a range of specific on-field metrics.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: For example, when Jeremy Doku was signed in 2023 , then manager Pep Guardiola decided he wanted a winger who was direct, akin to Leroy Sane, because at the time they had Jack Grealish and Riyad Mahrez, who preferred to keep the ball and cut inside.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Among the criteria applied in City's brief were the following: making (running into) the box, pressure regains, take-on percentage and opposition-half pressure.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Doku's overall numbers ticked the boxes Guardiola was looking for, although the Belgian's 'making the box' score was among his lowest readings.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Since his arrival, Doku has improved this rating - an example City say shows how their data systems are helping to improve existing players.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: There is also a 'utilisation chart' that records how often the player has been used over a three-year period, as well as a scouting grade that indicates how highly the traditional scouts rate the individual.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Each player is also awarded an overall "current impact score" - which predicts what impression he would be expected to make immediately on signing - and a "potential impact score" that projects the contribution the player could make in the future.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Perhaps the most intriguing reading on the acquisition packs is a player's "action value score".
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: This positions them in a league table that includes City players and ones from rival clubs who play in a similar role.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Once the acquisition reports are evaluated, the list is further reduced to 2-3 players once City's valuation of the player has been factored in.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Data contributes heavily to the price range City believe a player falls in, and the valuation is never a single number.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: A decision is then made on which player is the priority, though all players on the shortlist are worked on simultaneously in the event of changing circumstances, for example if a player becomes unavailable.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Indeed, being able to move according to the market is something the data team feel they have become adept at.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The sudden emergence of Yan Diomande last season led to City completing checks on him before he joined Real Madrid from RB Leipzig.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The club also paid close attention to Eduardo Camavinga's metrics in case Real decided to sell a midfielder.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: This video can not be played How Man City used data to sign Anderson Anderson was an obvious signing for a top Premier League club.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The 23-year-old had developed into a key player for Nottingham Forest .
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: An added appeal was the fact he is English, and had cemented his position in the national team.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: City fought off other top clubs, including Manchester United , to sign him .
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: It would seem, on the face of it, a straightforward decision.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: But the way City analysed it underlines their incredibly forensic approach even when, outwardly, it might be considered they did not need to be so comprehensive given Anderson's obvious talents.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The fact they still used their algorithm and went through all their normal steps says a lot about elite football in the modern day - and also the limitations of data alone.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: That is because - perhaps surprisingly - Anderson's metrics didn't necessarily catch the eye.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: At the start of last season, despite emerging uncertainty over Guardiola's future, the club knew they would be in the market for at least one central midfielder come the summer.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: They knew Bernardo Silva was leaving while there were doubts over the futures of Rodri and Nico Gonzalez.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: There was an acknowledgement that replacing Silva and Rodri like-for-like would be virtually impossible, so they looked for a player who was equally adept at building play from either deep or high central midfield.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: As last season developed, doubt also emerged over the future of Tijjani Reijnders - but Enzo Fernandez was viewed as the favoured replacement for the Dutchman.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Anderson made the initial cut from the 650,000-man database to the longlist - but was not high in that group.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: However, his metric readings didn't immediately scream out the "no-brainer" he ultimately became.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: As City took a closer look, there was an acknowledgement Anderson's case does highlight some of the limitations of data.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Anderson did not score lots of goals for Forest, or consistently provide assists.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Because, generally speaking, Forest aren't a possession team like City, his general metrics in their algorithm did not grab the attention.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: With that in mind, City's data analysts had to consider that, because Anderson was generally playing closer to his own goal than he would at City, he wasn't getting the opportunities to impress in the final third of the pitch.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: So they paid close attention to what he was doing at Forest and modelled his potential role in a City team that generally plays closer to the opposition's goal,  dominates possession and has more elite players.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Among the criteria graded on Anderson's 'radar chart' were defensive regains, duel success, line-breaking passes, aerial-duel success and defensive errors.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: With his reading for defensive errors, it was acknowledged that, because Forest were a transitional side, some were a result of the area of the pitch in which he was asked to operate.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: He may, for example, have regained possession deep inside his own half but lost the ball because he had to play a longer and a riskier pass after being asked to play forward quickly.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: In the same scenario at City, it is anticipated Anderson would have options to play a shorter pass with a greater success rate.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: "Just because a player doesn't have the opportunity to perform a particular action on a regular basis because of the team he is playing doesn't mean he can't do it," said a source.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Anderson's data readings improved significantly as the season developed, which compelled the club's scouts to watch him on a regular basis.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: He stood up very favourably against City's existing midfielders - and a list of rival players the club had identified as possible signings in that area.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The results of the diligence completed by City's data team, scouts and other experts meant that even though Anderson's price increased beyond what City believed was his true valuation, they felt the risk was low.

sentences.text: "Elliot Anderson is a great example of how the process works," Viana said.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The initial recommendation came from scouts, and given Alvarez was not a player originally identified by his metrics, the data team had to take a closer look.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: Because the Argentine league isn't recognised as one of the strongest globally, City's general data settings mean players will reach a natural ceiling with their readings in comparison to those playing in one of Europe's top five divisions.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: So, City dug deeper into Alvarez's stats, and his impact on both the ball and River's scorelines.
sentences.article_title: How Man City overhauled their squad from a 650,000-strong database

sentences.text: The stats showed he was by far the best player in the Argentine top flight, and City believed they had enough evidence to say he would develop into a starter for a top-half club in one of Europe's top five leagues within two-and-half years.

sentences.text: The data model valued Alvarez between £26m and £40m.

sentences.text: City signed him for £14m so believed they were signing an undervalued player.

sentences.text: They eventually sold him to Atletico Madrid in 2024 for £81m.

sentences.text: It's the place where points are lost and never to be seen again, according to a popular social media meme.

sentences.text: Draw a line from Brighton to Bournemouth to Brentford and back down to Brighton again and you will have formed the Premier League's very own "Bermuda Triangle".
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Those three clubs have developed a reputation for taking points off the traditional Big Six - Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Manchester City , Manchester United and Tottenham .
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Recent results have only fuelled the narrative and helped to push the tongue-in-cheek theory.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: On Friday night, Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0 .
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Bournemouth , meanwhile, pushed Liverpool all the way before falling to a 1-0 defeat, with Alisson forced into a brilliant recovery stop to deny the Cherries an early opener.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Those are the sort of performances that stick in supporters' minds and help explain why the theory has taken hold.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Brighton have been the best-performing non-traditional Big Six side against Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Manchester City , Manchester United and Spurs, taking 42 points from 26 games - an average of 1.62 points per match.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: The Cherries are not far behind, collecting 35 points from 26 matches, or 1.35 points per game.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Brentford , however, have taken 22 points from 26 matches, averaging 0.85 points per game.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Newcastle (1.46), Nottingham Forest (1.46) and Aston Villa (1.38) have all outperformed the Bees against the traditional Big Six over the same period.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: In other words, the clubs most commonly grouped together by the meme have produced very different levels of success against elite opposition.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Brighton and Bournemouth have consistently taken points off the Premier League's heavyweights.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Brentford 's record is less convincing.
sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.article_title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith was the only South African to win a gold medal at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris Having ended a two-year exile from competitive swimming, South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith has revealed she "lost the love" for her sport before stepping away from the pool in 2024.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The 29-year-old's decision to retire straight after the Paris Games came as a surprise, given she had just won 200m breaststroke gold in the French capital to add to her 100m title from Tokyo 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: But after two years away, which included several months in which she did not swim at all, Smith says she is now "free from the things that made me hate swimming".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "My whole life, I was kind of a robot towards swimming," she told Newsday on the BBC World Service.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "You're so zoned in, you're obsessed with something, so there isn't actually time for you to think about things outside of the pool that you potentially have a passion for.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think probably everyone would think that the timing [of retirement] was the worst.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Smith on retirement and becoming South Africa’s most decorated Olympian But despite making history for her country, Smith says financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, also contributed to her decision to retire.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The financial burden on any athlete is so tough," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I relied on my parents funding me until I broke the world record at the Olympics.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: And then, all of a sudden, now people are interested in maybe sponsoring you.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But the majority of sponsorships for athletes are based on performance.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: So then you have that pressure and expectation to always have to perform, otherwise you're not going to get paid.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think the financial side, and also being in a system where they're not really putting the athletes first, made it really difficult." Smith won her first Olympic title under her maiden name Schoenmaker, before changing her surname when she married sports agent Joel Smith in 2023.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The marriage made her part of a wider South African sporting dynasty, given that her sister-in-law is Rachel Smith, who was married to Springboks captain Siya Kolisi before their split.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith admits her own marriage changed the way she thought about her future.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Thinking about families as a woman, you have to time it perfectly, because if you're pregnant, it's not like you can still compete." While children are not yet part of her journey, Smith says working out what to do next was far from easy.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I definitely understand what athletes mean from the post-Olympic depression," said the 2023 200m breaststroke world champion, who also counts Commonwealth and African titles among her achievements.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was such an emptiness in my life, because my whole life revolved around swimming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I don't have to eat at a certain time, I don't have to sleep at a certain time, I don't have to think about travelling or not spending time with family anymore.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The world is so overwhelming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's like, in which direction to go?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was definitely the toughest season that I had to go through.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I think it's probably why it's made me a stronger person." Smith married her husband Joel in November 2023 and says family life was one of the reasons behind her decision to retire Initially, Smith took on speaking engagements to pay the bills.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: She smiles when she admits: "I hate public speaking.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I hate being in front of people." The same cannot be said of her love for competition.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Having returned to the pool in order to keep fit, she decided to have a crack at triathlon, something she describes as a "crazy idea".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The training was so intense, and I was like, 'OK, I might as well just go back to swimming if I'm going to train this hard'," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Every time I went back to the swimming pool and I dived in, I was like, 'Yeah, this is a feeling that I really miss so much'.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think slowly over the year and a half, I just realised 'Wow, I really do love swimming'." Having made her decision to come out of retirement, Smith now wants to freshen things up and "try something new".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: That means a change to the 50m breaststroke, an event which has just been added to the Olympic schedule for the first time ahead of the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I thought, 'Why don't I try?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Why don't I give myself that challenge?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Reinvent myself'," said Smith.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I always try and describe it to someone that maybe doesn't understand swimming; it's like a 400m runner and a 100m [runner].
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's two different body types, two different trainings, and that's where I'm going." It means she has more than halved her training volume, with three sessions a week instead of eight - a change she believes will help her retain her love for her sport and live a more balanced life.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I feel like I'm being so lazy because I used to do 12km per day and now the focus is on taking time to be as explosive as possible.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Now I'm doing 12km over a whole week.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I have 20 years of endurance in my pocket, but I can definitely see I don't have those fast twitch [muscle] fibres.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's a whole different way of teaching my body how to swim." Those initial 20 years in the pool left Smith feeling burned out.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Now she says she has earned the right to do things on her terms.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Swimming was an opportunity given to me by my parents and I believe I took it on full heartedly.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But, for the first time, it's my decision whether I want to come back.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I've achieved way more than I ever dreamed in my whole life, so I have nothing to prove." BBC African Sports Personality of the Year 2021: Tatjana Schoenmaker profile.

sentences.text: Real Madrid have won six out of seven matches in all competitions this season Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe says he stands "in full solidarity with Ceuta" after choosing to obscure a message of support for people who live in the Spanish enclave.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Real players wore T-shirts carrying the message 'Todos somos Caballas' - 'We are all Caballas' - before Tuesday's match against Elche.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Caballas is a nickname for the people of Ceuta - a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast, bordering Morocco and separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: More than 100 people died when tens of thousands of migrants crossed into the territory from neighbouring Morocco in July.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Mbappe - along with team-mates Vinicius Jr and Ibrahima Konate - rolled up their shirts to partially cover up the message.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I want to explain this clearly so people understand," the France international said.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It was the clubs' decision to include the T-shirt and to have us wear it.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: We players had to wear it.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "The first thing I want to say is that I stand in full solidarity with Ceuta and with all the victims.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "Because before I'm a player, I'm a human being.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "But I also wanted to make a gesture and spare a thought for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in harsh condition." Mbappe acknowledged his gesture could be misunderstood.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It wasn't an easy position to take," he said.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It was difficult because, in the end, people might think I'm against the people of Ceuta.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I have nothing against them, and I support them 100% in my thoughts.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: But I also wanted to spare a thought for all the people who are suffering because, at the end of the day, I'm human, and I don't want to prioritise one form of suffering over another.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "There are people who are suffering, and it breaks my heart to see that happening in the world.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: I'm a young man who wants the best for the world we live in.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I aim to send a message of positivity and peace, and I hope this situation is resolved quickly." This is not the first time Real Madrid have shown support for Ceuta.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Before their Champions League meeting with Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu on 8 September, supporters in the south stand displayed cards featuring the coat of arms of the autonomous city, while the rest of the stadium joined the tribute with a round of applause.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: The initiative was part of a wider show of support for Ceuta, after at least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest there.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Locals have expressed safety concerns and some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Tuesday's pre-match gesture to show support for the territory also highlighted the differing approaches among players and clubs to the Ceuta campaign.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Barcelona did not take part in the initiative, though players at other La Liga fixtures wore the shirts as intended.

sentences.text: This video can not be played How two Scots ended up playing for Uganda Teenage brothers Olly and Seb Fisher are closing in on their dream of international recognition - but it won't come from their homeland of Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Instead, the Partick Thistle duo are in line to play for Uganda.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: They believe they would become the first white players ever to represent the African nation, thanks to their mother Kate being born there.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "My gran and grandad lived out here for, I think, four or five years," Olly, 18, tells BBC Sport Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "My grandfather came out here to teach in a school then my mum was born here.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: So, it's a bit of a strange one." The siblings became aware of interest from Uganda about six months ago, following a chance conversation some time before between their father and a football consultant at a game in Nigeria.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: And, at the start of August, they were invited to attend under-20 and under-17s training camps.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: They spent last week in Jinja in the country's eastern region and will stay on for one more week, with the pair saying they're "shocked" and "honoured" at the call-ups.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "I couldn't believe it," 16-year-old striker Seb said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "It's one of those things you look at and you're shocked.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Most other people couldn't as well." Goalkeeper Olly had a similar reaction.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "A real mixture of emotions," he said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: I didn't really think that this was a possibility but I was honoured to be asked to represent Uganda.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: I thought it was a real big opportunity." Mum Kate is "ecstatic" and "thinks it'd be a great experience for us", adds Seb.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Olly Fisher, second right, with his Ugandan team-mates There is another Scottish link with Uganda, with former Hearts and Ghana midfielder Laryea Kingston currently coach of Uganda's under-20s.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: And he is the one who believes the Fisher brothers are on the verge of making history.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "Coach Kingston was saying we'd be the first white boys to play for Uganda, which would be history in the making," Seb explained.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "It is very special." And Olly added: "It's never been done before, so definitely it is very special." The pair feel like they're making connections with the African nation, having been reared on stories about Uganda from their grandparents.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: And even though they have been training in oppressively warm conditions, they are embracing the opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "Everyone has been brilliant, welcoming, really great," Seb said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "The other boys have been brand new with us.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Some of the boys actually come from the same area where my mum was born.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: So, they were all talking about that." The boys will return to Scotland soon, combining training and playing with Thistle with university and school, but are planning to rejoin their new international team-mates in the near future.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Olly hopes to be part of his squad if they qualify for the Under-20's Africa Cup of Nations early next year, and Seb could be in the Under-17 squad for November's World Cup in Qatar.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "That's what you want as a footballer, being in an international environment," Seb said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "It makes you a better player and hopefully it does for the two of us, and I think it will, and benefit us very much going back to Scotland playing at Thistle." The Fisher brothers with Uganda Under-20s head coach and former Hearts player Laryea Kingston

sentences.text: President Donald Trump has infused his ongoing feud with the White House press with a new level of acrimony.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Journalists from three major media outlets - CNN, Politico and MS Now - were denied access and had their press credentials confiscated on Saturday morning as they attempted to enter the White House grounds for work.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: As media watchdog organisations and the White House Correspondents Association cry foul, Trump appears set to press ahead with a sweeping effort to punish these outlets.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: In his Truth Social post announcing his decision on Friday, he said he was "banning" the organisations because "of their constant 'reporting' of fake news".
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: In remarks later that day, he complained that "something is wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories".
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: "If they want to write them, that's fine," he continued.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: "I don't have to let them into the people's house", he said, referring to the White House.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Journalists denied White House access after Trump banned some media outlets The president's frustration at the media, however, came after a week of setbacks in which major institutions handed him a series of losses across his agenda.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: First, the Supreme Court blocked his plan to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterms.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: This prompted Trump to lash out at the court's justices including those he had appointed.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: "These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court," he said.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: The Federal Reserve, the US central bank, then raised interest rates after Trump had spent months arguing they should be cut.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: This was followed by a judge ordering his administration to give 30 days' notice before making any changes to the Kennedy Center arts venue in Washington DC after the president warned it could be "ripped down".
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: These headlines, combined with approval ratings that recently sunk to record lows for his second term, suggest Trump is facing challenging political headwinds.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: His latest attack on the press, however, raises clear legal questions.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: The First Amendment to the US Constitution forbids Congress from "abridging" the freedom of the press.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: It is language that courts have long interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: All three targeted news outlets have promised to file lawsuits challenging Trump's decision.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Although the breadth of this move is unprecedented, it is far from the first time the Trump administration has attempted to limit or deny access to the White House to members of mainstream media outlets.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: In his first term, the administration revoked CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press credentials, setting off a legal battle that was ultimately resolved in the journalist's favour.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: It also temporarily suspended the pass of a reporter who had a heated argument with White House adviser Sebastian Gorka – a move that also was subsequently blocked by the courts.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: That dispute also led to a protracted - and yet to be fully resolved - legal battle, prompting the White House to change press pool rules to drop the guaranteed spot for all wire services.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Trump says ban on some news outlets from White House is "because they're fake news" The White House bans, however, represent a dramatic escalation.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: The restrictions include access to the entirety of the White House grounds, not just the press pool.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: And they target entire news organisations, not just a single disfavoured correspondent.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: At the moment, however, the president is embattled.

sentences.text: Even beyond the week of clear setbacks, he is in the midst of an unpopular and difficult-to-resolve war of choice in Iran, which has led to a surge in energy and other consumer prices, deflating his standing with the American public.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: Polls also suggest his party faces an uphill battle to retain control of the House of Representatives and perhaps the Senate in November's crucial midterm congressional elections.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.text: His attempts to improve the public's mood by touting his accomplishments in campaign events and at his Republican Party's convention earlier this month in Texas have, at least so far, proven ineffective.
sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks

sentences.article_title: Trump escalates media fight after week of setbacks
